title_idea: EU FDI Screening Rules Apply from 17 January 2028; 12% of 2025 Cases Needed In-Depth Review
keyword: EU FDI screening rules apply 17 January 2028 in-depth review
angle: An importer planning an EU acquisition or other foreign investment can use the 15-day closure pattern and 12% in-depth-review share to set schedule contingency before the FISR applies on 17 January 2028; the figures are aggregate screening caseload statistics, not a per-shipment duty or fee.

figures.unit: increase in notifications to the EU cooperation mechanism
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: the number of notifications to the EU’s cooperation mechanism increased by 40% between 2024 and 2025

figures.unit: foreign direct investments notified to the Commission
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: In 2025, EU Member States notified 667 investments to the Commission, up from 477 notifications in 2024.

figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: In 2025, EU Member States notified 667 investments to the Commission, up from 477 notifications in 2024.

figures.unit: share of notified cases closed within 15 days
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: Of the 667 cases notified, 88% were closed within 15 days.

figures.unit: calendar days within which most notified cases were closed
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: Of the 667 cases notified, 88% were closed within 15 days.

figures.unit: share of notified investments requiring an in-depth security risk assessment
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: 12% of the investments notified to the Commission required an in-depth security risk assessment – a 4% rise compared to last year.

figures.unit: manufacturing share of in-depth assessment cases
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: Most such cases were in manufacturing, which accounted for 53% of all transactions (up from 50% in 2024).

figures.unit: share of cases in which the Commission issued opinions
figures.source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security
figures.evidence: In keeping with 2024 and 2023, the Commission issued opinions in less than 2% of cases.

sources: European Commission (Directorate-General for Trade and Economic Security), “Screening of foreign direct investment continues to advance EU security and public order,” 14 October 2026.
